lights.title: Health lights
lights.tapHint: Tap a light to see what it means.

cash.name: Cash
cash.ask: How long can you run on cash?
cash.explain: Cash runway: how many months the company can pay its bills before the cash runs out.
cash.G: Profitable, or 12 months or more of cash.

customers.name: Customers
customers.ask: How many pay, and how many stay?
customers.explain: Net customers and retention: are more paying customers arriving than leaving, and how many stay?
customers.G: More customers arriving than leaving, and 75% or more stay.
customers.R: Losing more customers than it wins, or few sign-ups pay.

debt.name: Debt
debt.explain: Debt and interest cover: can profit pay the interest, and is debt growing faster than profit?
debt.G: No debt, or profit pays the interest 3 times or more.
debt.A: Profit pays the interest 1.5 to 3 times.
debt.R: Interest is hard to cover, or debt is growing while margin falls.

ceo.name: CEO
ceo.explain: Insider trades: has the CEO been selling shares lately?
ceo.G: No share sales in the last 3 quarters.
ceo.A: One sale in the last 3 quarters.
ceo.R: Sales in 2 or more of the last 3 quarters.

detail.customers: {{pct}}% of customers stay. Net change this quarter: {{net}}.
detail.ceoNone: No share sales in the last 3 quarters.
detail.ceoSales: {{n}} share sales in the last 3 quarters.

pitch.tip: You can invest without asking anything. Asking costs nothing, and you learn from the answers.

trade.gainLoss: Gain or loss on this part
trade.whyHint: Pick one. It is not marked right or wrong. It helps you look back later.
trade.notEnough: Not enough cash for the minimum.
trade.jailed: You sat out this turn after selling in a panic. You cannot buy until next turn.

portfolio.title: Your properties
portfolio.empty: You do not own anything yet. Land on an Auction tile to hear a pitch.
portfolio.noSell: This company has failed. Its shares are worth nothing.
portfolio.concentration: Concentration warning: {{pct}}% of your invested money is in {{sector}}.
portfolio.colourNote: Colour sets: owning a lot in one sector is a risk marker.

quarterResults.title: Quarter {{n}} results
quarterResults.none: Nothing to report. You do not own any companies yet.

ev.downRound: sold new shares at a lower price (a down-round)
ev.failed: ran out of cash and shut down
ev.rumourSpike: price jumped on a wave of excitement

rent.note: Rent is the company's profit share this quarter. Results are not guaranteed.

bank.intro: The Banker has two things to offer today.
bank.clueBody: Pick a company and a light. The Banker tells you the real answer, free.
bank.loanBody: Costs ₹600 interest every quarter. You can repay any time and must clear it by quarter 12. Borrowing makes gains and losses bigger.
bank.loanHave: You already have a loan of {{x}}.
bank.repayShort: Not enough cash to repay yet.

emergency.title: Pay ₹25,000 now
emergency.body: Your family needs ₹25,000 by the end of this quarter. If your cash is short, you will have to sell something.
emergency.short: You are {{x}} short. Sell a property below, then pay.
emergency.payShortNote: You cannot cover all of it. The rest becomes a loan.

lesson.replayUsed: You have used this year's replay.
lesson.replayHint: Go back to the start of this quarter and decide again. Same market, same luck.
lesson.calm: Calm and curious: this is about what the data showed, not about being wrong.

yearEnd2.none: No houses yet. Each ₹10,000 paid into a property adds one.

report.title: Your judgement report
report.cleared: Stage cleared. Your lamp is lit.
report.notCleared: Not cleared yet. Replay and try new questions.

research.name: Research
research.body: Did you ask before you invested?

skepticism.name: Skepticism
skepticism.body: Did you spot the risky companies in time?

spread.name: Spread
spread.body: Was your money spread across different sectors?

calm.name: Calm and patience
calm.body: Did you stay steady in a falling market?

habits.name: Money habits
habits.body: Fees, a cushion for emergencies, idle cash.

report.profitNote: Shown for information. It never decides the result.
report.luck: You finished ahead, but part of that was luck. Here is what to repeat and what not to.
report.unlucky: You finished behind, but much of your method was sound. Luck decides some quarters.
report.toolkitBody: Real-life terms you met through your own decisions.
report.toolkitNone: Play a few quarters to earn terms for your toolkit.
report.flipsLine: You asked about {{n}} lights per purchase on average.
report.concLine: Most money in one sector at once: {{p}}%.
report.closing: Real markets are harder than this game. This teaches how to ask good questions, not what to buy.
